# Turn Your Messy Meeting Notes into a Clean To-Do List with Qwen

> **In short:** Paste your rough meeting notes into Qwen and ask it to pull out action items, owners, and deadlines. You'll get a tidy list you can copy straight into an email or team chat.

After a long meeting, your notes usually look like a brain dump — half-sentences, names misspelled, and a deadline buried somewhere in paragraph three. Qwen is an AI assistant made by Alibaba that can read a wall of messy text and pull out the parts that matter. By the end of this guide, you'll have a clean action list ready to share in minutes, not a re-typing session that eats your whole afternoon.

## Before you start
- A Qwen account, which you can create with an email on the Qwen website. The basic service is free to use, though some features may sit behind a paid plan — check the current pricing page for details.
- Your meeting notes ready to paste: typed, voice-dictated, or transcribed from a photo. Even rough shorthand works.
- About 10 minutes total, including reading the guide.

## Step 1 — Open Qwen and start a fresh chat
Go to the Qwen website in your browser and sign in. Once you're in, look for a button like **"New chat"** or a **+** icon, usually at the top of the sidebar or above the message box. Click it so you begin with an empty conversation — this keeps things tidy and avoids mixing your meeting notes with an earlier topic.

If you don't see a clear "New chat" option, try refreshing the page; many AI tools treat a blank page as a fresh start by default. On the phone app, the **+** is usually in the top corner.

You'll know it worked when the message box is empty and there's no history of a previous conversation shown above it.

## Step 2 — Paste your messy notes into the chat
Tap or click inside the empty message box at the bottom of the screen, then paste your raw meeting notes — typed, voice-transcribed, or even shorthand is fine. Watch the text appear in the box the same way it would in any chat app. Don't worry yet about cleaning anything up; the whole point is to let Qwen do that work for you.

If pasting fails or the box seems stuck, try copying the notes in smaller chunks (a paragraph at a time) or switching browsers. Some meeting notes get very long, and splitting them helps Qwen handle them more reliably.

💬 Example: "Tuesday meeting — discussed Q3 launch. Maria will handle budget, by Friday. John drafts the email for next week. Sarah to book venue for the offsite — not sure when. Need to follow up with design team about the logo. Pricing still undecided, ask Tom."

You'll know it worked when your notes show up in the message box and the **Send** button (often a paper-plane or arrow icon) becomes active.

## Step 3 — Ask Qwen to pull out the action items
Below your pasted notes, type a clear instruction — what AI assistants call a **prompt**, which is just a fancy word for "what you ask the AI to do." The clearer your prompt, the better the result. Tell Qwen what you want and what format you want it in.

After you hit send, Qwen will spend a few seconds thinking, then write back a structured response — usually a numbered or bulleted list. If the answer comes back as one long paragraph, just ask in the next step to redo it as a list.

💬 Example: "From the notes above, pull out every action item. For each one, list the task, the person responsible (if mentioned), and any deadline. Format as a clean numbered list."

You'll know it worked when Qwen's reply contains a structured list with names and tasks pulled out of your messy notes.

## Step 4 — Refine the list with a follow-up
Qwen's first answer is rarely perfect. Read it carefully — you'll likely want to add a deadline column, group tasks by owner, or simplify the language. Just type another message in the same chat asking for the change. Qwen remembers the earlier notes and reply, so it can rewrite the list without you re-pasting anything.

If the response is too long, ask for a shorter version. If something important is missing, point it out and Qwen usually catches it on the second try. Keep adjusting until the list reads the way you'd write it yourself.

💬 Example: "Now group the list by person so each owner has their tasks under their name. If a deadline isn't clear, write 'no deadline given' instead of guessing."

You'll know it worked when the revised list looks like something you'd be happy to send to your team without further editing.

## Step 5 — Copy the final list
Once you're happy with the result, it's time to grab it. Click and drag your mouse across Qwen's reply to highlight the text, then press **Ctrl+C** (Windows) or **Cmd+C** (Mac). On a phone, tap and hold the text until selection handles appear, then choose **Copy**.

If your version of Qwen has a small **Copy** button near the reply, use that — it usually copies everything cleanly in one go. After copying, the list is now stored on your device's clipboard, ready to paste anywhere.

You'll know it worked when you can paste the text into any other app and see your clean action list appear.

## Step 6 — Share it with your team
Open your team chat (Slack, Teams, a group email, whatever your team uses) and paste the list with a short message. A friendly line like "Here are the action items from today's meeting — let me know if I missed anything" works well and invites quick corrections.

One important honesty note: Qwen cannot send the message for you or post tasks into your project tracker automatically. It only helped you draft and clean the list. The sending step is still yours, by hand or through your usual tools.

You'll know it worked when your team replies, reacts, or jumps into action — and you didn't have to retype a single messy note.

## Common mistakes
- **Pasting without any instructions.** Qwen needs to know what you want. Just dumping notes rarely produces a useful list — always add a prompt like "pull out action items."
- **Trusting the first answer blindly.** Always read the list back. AI can misattribute a task to the wrong person when notes are ambiguous, and a 30-second check saves confusion later.
- **Forgetting to mention the format.** If you want a numbered list, a table, or items grouped by person, say so. Without that hint, Qwen picks a format for you, and you may not like it.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Even outside work, this trick works for parent-teacher meetings, medical appointments, or family planning — anywhere someone rattles off "things to do" and you need a clean list afterwards.
- **For your business or work:** You can turn a 30-minute note-cleaning session into a 2-minute copy-paste. Multiply that across a week of meetings and the saved time adds up fast.
- **If you're just getting started:** Try it once on your last meeting's notes — you probably still have them somewhere. Seeing a clean list appear from your own messy scribbles is the moment it clicks.

## Try it now
Find the last meeting you had — even a quick 10-minute one — and paste those notes into Qwen with the prompt: *"Pull out every action item, who owns it, and any deadline. Format as a numbered list."* See what you get back in under two minutes.
